segments.text: Do you ever feel like you know all the words, but you cannot make a sentence?
Have you noticed that when you try to speak, the words get stuck in your head?
But when you open your mouth, nothing comes out.
Or maybe you speak, but the sentence sounds wrong.
I see this problem every day.
Students come to me and say, "Mark, I know thousands of words.
And the answer is not what they expect.
Today, I will show you what is really happening.
And more importantly, I will show you how to fix it.
But first, let me tell you about John.
John is a student from Spain.
He learns new words on his phone.
But when he tries to speak, he feels like a beginner.
Because John learns English like a mathematician.
He builds sentences in his head step by step.
While John is building his sentence, the conversation continues.
The problem is not John's vocabulary.
The problem is not John's grammar.
The problem is the way he builds sentences.
You are in a coffee shop.
A foreigner sits next to you.
He smiles and says, "Hi, how are you?"
Then he asks, "Is this your first time here?"
But now you must build a new sentence.
In your head you start subject I verb is am I am come came coming Wait.
You say, "Yes, I I I am The foreigner looks confused.
This has happened to you, right?
But it is not your fault.
Your brain is working too hard.
And that is why you struggle.
Native speakers do not build sentences.
Let me say that again. Native [snorts] speakers do not build sentences.
When you build a house, you do not make every brick.
Native speakers have ready-made chunks, ready-made phrases, ready-made sentence patterns.
That is why they speak fast.
That is why they sound natural.
That is why you do not need to think.
You do not need to learn more words.
You need to learn how native speakers put words together.
This is the discovery that changes everything.
And it makes English feel natural.
So, how do you start building sentences like a native speaker?
Here are three simple ways to improve today.
Number one, learn phrases, not words.
For example, do not learn the word need.
Learn the phrase I need to.
Do not learn the word want.
Learn the phrase I want to.
Do not learn the word think.
Learn the phrase I think that.
Now, you can make many sentences.
This is how native speakers do it.
It's plus adjective plus two plus verb.
I'm plus verb ing plus to plus verb.
I can can plus verb plus if plus sentence.
I can understand if you speak slowly.
I can help if you ask me.
I can learn if I practice every day.
You put in the ingredients, you get a perfect sentence.
Learn the patterns, use the patterns.
This is the most important tip.
When you hear a phrase many times, it becomes automatic.
Your brain will say, "I've heard this before.
And the words will come out naturally, easily, quickly.
Mistakes are part of the journey.
Every mistake is a step forward.
See you in the next lesson.
